answer: Copying the same citations across 101 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 101 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the plume index resolves every citation against the pigment checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the wander audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 2683 identities would post 1301 proofs and burn roughly 76 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
